editorial:
The Red House is a 1947 Sol Lesser production released by United Artists, directed by Delmer Daves and starring Edward G. Robinson. Miklos Rozsa is credited with the score. It is a noir-flavored rural thriller that fits horror and noir programs.

The print status is not settled. The 1947 film's renewal window ran through 1975, and OCR searches of the catalog volumes for 1974, 1975 and 1976 found no renewal. That is negative evidence only: the 1947 registration was not found and the renewal pages were not read one by one. Treat the film as likely public domain, not verified. The novel by George Agnew Chamberlain was not checked, nor was any separate music publication. Any commercial Blu-ray or DVD may add new material, so check the source of any copy before reuse.
faq: Was the copyright on The Red House renewed?

No renewal turned up in OCR text searches of the Catalog of Copyright Entries Motion Pictures volumes for 1974, 1975 and 1976, which cover the window for a 1947 film. The 1947 registration was not found and the pages were not read one by one, so verify against the page images if you need certainty.
Can I use a Blu-ray or DVD copy of The Red House?

Safer to avoid commercial discs unless you have checked them. A faithful transfer adds no film copyright, but commercial releases may include new titles, extras or other added material that is protected, and ripping a copy-protected disc can violate 17 U.S.C. 1201.
